Subject: New payee / treasury details after merger

Hi Grace —

Following our closing last week, the finance team at AcquirerCo has consolidated treasury and requested that all invoices for the Cobalt Health product be remitted to the new entity (AcquirerCo Treasury). We need to confirm where Redwood should send invoices and whether Redwood can accept payee updates for the existing subscription (INV-2026-09-1127).

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood reissue outstanding invoices to the new legal payee and remit address?
- Can you add the new treasury email (treasury@cobalthealth.com) to invoice notifications?

I've attached the signed MOA and the treasury wiring stub for your team. Please let me know any KYC or vendor update forms you need.

Thanks —
Samantha Brooks
Head of Finance Operations
Cobalt Health
attachments: Signed-MOA_Cobalt-Acquirer.pdf, Cobalt_Treasury_Wiring_Instructions.pdf

Subject: RE: New payee / treasury details after merger

Hi Samantha —

Congrats on closing. We can support reissuing invoices and routing future invoices to the new treasury address, but we have a couple internal checks to complete before we can switch the payee:

1) We need a remittance authorization from AcquirerCo (signed) or confirmation from an authorized signatory. The signed MOA helps but we typically ask for a short vendor-change authorization on company letterhead.

2) Our finance team needs the tax/VAT registration for the new payee (if applicable) and the remit address to populate billing headers.

If you can share that authorization (or confirm who at AcquirerCo will sign), we can:
- reissue INV-2026-09-1127 to AcquirerCo Treasury and send a credit note to the prior payee,
- add treasury@cobalthealth.com to invoice notifications, and
- update our billing contact and remit instructions for future invoices.

I'll loop in our finance lead — Marissa and Ben, can you advise on required documentation and turnaround?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Account Lead, Enterprise Care
Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.inference.com>, ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 18:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: New payee / treasury details after merger

Grace —

Finance checklist:
- Signed vendor change request on AcquirerCo letterhead (preferably with a company stamp or signatory block).
- New payee legal name and Tax ID (or VAT registration) for invoice header.
- Bank / wiring instructions (we have the stub Samantha attached — ok as long as it matches their legal entity).
- Confirmation of who will receive invoices (treasury@cobalthealth.com is fine, please confirm if copies to procurement@acquirerco.com are needed).

If all docs are in order we can reissue the invoice within 2 business days and mark the old invoice as superseded with a credit note. For recurring billing we'll change the ledger mapping so new invoices are billed to AcquirerCo Treasury starting with the next cycle (billing date 2026-09-30).

Aditya — can you prepare the credit note template and check whether any VAT registration crosswalk is required for the current customer record?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: New payee / treasury details after merger

Marissa / team —

I reviewed the MOA and the wiring stub. Two notes for the VAT/tax side:
- Cobalt Health currently sits on our US account with no VAT registration. If AcquirerCo provides a new Tax ID (EIN) we will update the invoice header. No VAT crosswalk required for US->US entity move.
- If they intend to route payment via an EU treasury (different bank country), we need the bank country and VAT registration for invoicing to remain tax-compliant.

I've drafted a short vendor-change authorization template (attached) that should speed signoff. Once we receive the signed authorization and the official Tax ID, I'll queue the credit note and new invoice reissue.

Aditya Rao
Revenue Operations — Payments
Redwood Inference
